title: Missed FD Income: How to Rectify and What Happens If You Don't
description: Fixed Deposit (FD) interest income is fully taxable under Indian income tax laws. If you missed declaring FD interest in your original Income Tax Return (ITR).

faq.a: An ITR-U is a facility provided by the Income Tax Department allowing taxpayers to correct errors or declare additional income missed in their original or revised ITR within two years from the end of the relevant assessment year.

faq.q: How long do I have to file an ITR-U?
faq.a: You can file an ITR-U within two years from the end of the relevant assessment year. For example, for income earned in FY 2022-23 (AY 2023-24), you can file an ITR-U until March 31, 2026.

faq.q: What is the penalty for filing an ITR-U?
faq.a: The penalty depends on when you file. If filed within 12 months from the end of the assessment year, it's 25% of the aggregate tax and interest due. If filed between 12 and 24 months, it's 50%.

faq.q: Can I file an ITR-U to claim a refund?
faq.a: No, an ITR-U cannot be filed to reduce your total income, claim a refund, or increase a refund already claimed. It is specifically for declaring additional income and paying the corresponding tax.

faq.q: What if TDS was already deducted on my FD interest?
faq.a: Even if TDS was deducted by the bank, you still need to declare the full FD interest income in your ITR. TDS is an advance tax, and your final tax liability depends on your income slab. You can claim credit for the TDS paid.

faq.q: What happens if I don't rectify undeclared FD income?
faq.a: If the Income Tax Department discovers undeclared income, you could face scrutiny, higher penalties (up to 200% of the tax payable), interest on unpaid tax, and potentially prosecution in severe cases.
